To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the household production function framework cannot be used to measure welfare changes in a manner consistent with traditional welfare theory because the Marshallian demand functions are not well defined.

(a) the Marshallian demand functions are not unique; (b) Marshallian functions do not uniquely define Hicksian demand functions; (c) Marshallian functions cannot uniquely determine the direction of Hicksian demand function shifts, even if the Hicksian functions are defined; and (d) Marshallian functions can only bound compensating and equivalent variations.
(1) jointness in production implies that Marshallian functions are not uniquely defined, and therefore, (2) Marshallian functions cannot serve as the basis for exact welfare measures.

the welfare measurement problem in the household production approach is not simply one of estimating the appropriate parameters of the demand system, but rather one of determining the appropriate commodity prices to be used in the estimation procedure.
